message.content: Lions mate during the breeding season (typically late winter to early spring). A male will approach a receptive female, often after a brief sniffing or vocalization. If she accepts, they will engage in a short courtship ritual involving grooming and vocalizing. The actual copulation lasts only a few minutes, but it can happen multiple times over several days. After mating, the male may guard the female’s territory to protect her from rivals. The female then gives birth to a litter after a gestation period of about 110 days.
